title: Find K-Length Substrings With No Repeated Characters
statement:
Count the substrings of `s` whose length is exactly `k` and in which no character appears twice, and return that count.

- A substring is a contiguous run of characters; two substrings starting at different positions count separately even when they spell the same text.
- When `k` is longer than `s`, no such substring exists and the answer is `0`.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

The direct way slices out every length-`k` substring and checks it with a set, costing O(n·k). Neighbouring windows share all but two characters, so it is cheaper to slide one window of width `k` across `s` and keep a tally of its letters: each step adds one character on the right and drops one on the left. A window of `k` characters has no repeats exactly when it holds `k` different letters.

## Approach

1. Keep `count`, the number of times each letter appears in the window, and `distinct`, how many letters have a non-zero count.
2. Move `right` across `s`. Add `s[right]`; if its count was 0, `distinct` grows.
3. Once the window is wider than `k`, drop `s[left]` with `left = right - k`; if its count falls to 0, `distinct` shrinks.
4. The window now has at most `k` characters, so `distinct === k` means it is full and repeat-free; add one to `answer`.
5. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "havefunonleetcode"`, `k = 5`. At `right = 4` the window is `havef` with 5 distinct letters, so `answer = 1`. Sliding on, `avefu`, `vefun` and `efuno` also reach `distinct = 5` (`answer = 4`). From `funon` to `eetco` some letter appears twice, so `distinct` stays below 5. The last two windows `etcod` and `tcode` qualify again, giving `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each character enters and leaves the window once, and each step is constant work.
- Space: O(1): the tally has 26 slots whatever the input size.

## Pitfalls

- `k` may exceed `s.length` (or 26); the answer is then `0`, which the `distinct === k` test already gives without a special case.
- Update `distinct` only on the 0 → 1 and 1 → 0 transitions, not on every increment or decrement.
- Remove the character at `right - k` only when that index exists, otherwise the first windows lose letters they never had.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | occurrences of each letter in the current window |
| `distinct` | number of letters present in the window |
| `answer` | windows of length `k` found without repeats |
| `right` | index of the character entering the window |
| `left` | index of the character leaving the window |
| `added`, `removed` | letter indices (0–25) of those two characters |

narration.3: distinct counts the letters that currently appear at least once.
narration.6: Slide the right edge of the window across every character.
narration.8: A letter that was absent from the window adds a new distinct letter.
narration.11: Record the new character in the tally.
narration.13: The character k positions behind right is the one that falls out of the window.
narration.14: Only drop it once the window has grown past k characters.
narration.16: Remove the leaving character from the tally.
narration.17: If that was its last copy, the window has one distinct letter fewer.
narration.22: The window has at most k characters, so k distinct letters means it is full and has no repeats.
narration.26: Every window of length k has been checked; return the count.
